doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Algiers streetcars, the last horse car and the Naval Station
summary: Martin recalls the last horse car in 1899, when his aunt bought the horse, the electric cars from 1909 and across the river in 1911, and that the Naval Station was built right after the Spanish-American War.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Did they ever have street cars over there?
The last horse car run over there. Yeah. Then... That was 99, because my aunt bought the horse.
When they... When they put the...
When the horse was pulling out of that car, when they stopped the street car line, she bought the horse.
Oh, good. Yeah, you too. For me. Yeah.

Then they had... Then they had electric street cars, huh? Then they put the electric car, and it run from... 1909, from Brittany, to Connell Street Ferry, to Elmira and Newton. Then they put the Vyra out there. Yeah. Oh, yeah.
They put the Vyra out there. In 1911, that's when they put the car to run across the Vyra.
They had street cars going across there.

Then all the way down, and that's when they put the immigration station. Yeah, that's what I'm saying. Clay Dashie, man. Yeah. They put the electric car all the way down. Well, first, uh... The Short Lane. Yeah.
They go down... Was the Naval Station there then?
Yeah. The Naval Station had been there.
How long has that been there, that Naval? As long as you can remember, or did it come in later?
The Naval Station started when I was a little bit a boy, right after the Spanish American War. Right after that.
